headline: Deliveroo will start sending pavement robots to deliver takeaways and groceries in five parts of Britain.
score_reason: A named rollout with places and a supplier, but still weeks from the first delivery and limited to a few areas.
importance_line: Residents of Canary Wharf, Milton Keynes, Leeds, Stockton-on-Tees and Nottingham will share pavements with delivery robots, Deliveroo's 100,000 UK riders hear it is a complement not a replacement, and councils and pedestrian groups still decide how far it spreads.
summary: The Times reports, with the same details carried by Business Matters, that Deliveroo will begin pavement robot deliveries of food and groceries in the UK within weeks, starting in Canary Wharf in London and in Milton Keynes, Leeds, Stockton-on-Tees and Nottingham, using walking-pace robots from the US firm Coco. Chief executive Miki Kuusi said the robots are "not about replacing" riders but a cheaper complement for certain trips, while a pedestrian campaign group has already called rival Starship robots a danger on pavements.
notes: Text read on Business Matters; Times paywalled. machine_action false: rollout announced, first UK deliveries not yet made.
